headline: Bangladesh President Md. Shahabuddin may resign soon due to illness, successor talks begin
summary: Multiple sources indicate President Md. Shahabuddin may step down due to health reasons, prompting high-level discussions within the ruling BNP about his successor.
details: President Md. Shahabuddin may resign from his post very soon, with physical illness cited as a potential reason. Sources from both the government and the ruling BNP have confirmed that a high-level message regarding his resignation has already been conveyed.

Discussions are actively underway within the ruling BNP regarding his potential successor. A source close to the BNP's high command confirmed the high probability of the President's resignation in the near future.

A secretary currently holding a contractual government position has suddenly emerged as a prominent name for the next President. Previously, senior BNP leaders like Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain and Abdul Moyeen Khan were also considered.

If President Shahabuddin resigns, the Speaker will constitutionally assume presidential duties temporarily. A new President will then be elected by National Parliament members within the stipulated time frame, making the selection politically crucial.
The next national parliamentary election is expected to take place during the new President's term. This adds significant political weight to the ongoing discussions about who will fill the role.

While no official statement has been released by Bangabhaban or the government, a Bangabhaban-centric source indicates the President has hinted to his staff about leaving soon. He may take a period of rest and potentially travel abroad for treatment.

Md. Shahabuddin was sworn in as the 22nd President of Bangladesh on April 24, 2023, elected unopposed with the Awami League's nomination. His five-year term was originally set to conclude in April 2028.

His role became politically complex after the Awami League government's fall on August 5, 2024, following a student-people's uprising. Student leaders had demanded his removal, but the interim government did not act.

Following the subsequent national parliamentary election, the BNP came to power. Despite Shahabuddin's election under the previous government, the new BNP administration did not immediately move to remove him, though his future has been a subject of political discussion.

headline: AI forces popular Chinese actor to sell vegetables with grandfather after losing roles
summary: Shu Peng, known for his 'powerful CEO' roles in popular Chinese short dramas, found himself jobless as over 95% of new productions now use AI. He has since returned to his village to sell vegetables alongside his grandfather.
details: The rise of artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly impacting human jobs globally, with the entertainment industry now feeling the effects. Shu Peng, a 30-year-old Chinese actor known for his 'powerful CEO' roles in popular short dramas, has lost his acting career due to AI's influence.

The situation changed rapidly in early 2026, when approximately 122,000 out of 128,000 short dramas released in China's first quarter were created using AI. This means over 95% of newly released productions incorporated AI in some form, drastically reducing the need for human actors.

Once busy with a packed shooting schedule, Shu Peng suddenly found himself without acting work. After finishing his last short drama earlier this year, he left Hengdian, a major film production hub, and returned to his village in Shandong.
Recently, he was seen selling vegetables with his grandfather in the village market, a stark contrast to his on-screen persona. Relatives were surprised, while some fans sought him out for photos.

Despite the career change, Shu Peng remains optimistic. He told Chinese media that acting is just a profession, and if there's no acting work, he will find other ways to make a living honestly through hard work.

Shu Peng is not alone; reports suggest that the rise of AI in China's short drama industry has impacted nearly 2 million jobs. Actors who once earned up to 20,000 yuan (approx. $2,940 USD) daily now struggle to find work paying even 1,200 yuan.

AI is now integrated into almost all stages of drama production, from scriptwriting and character creation to modeling and post-production editing. This allows dramas to be produced in days at a much lower cost, compared to the longer, more expensive human-involved shoots.

However, Shu Peng has not given up on his acting dream. He plans to launch acting training programs and continue working on short dramas that feature real actors, acknowledging the tough reality of AI's undeniable impact on the creative industry.
